explanation: In France, pointing directly at someone or something with the index finger is considered rude and aggressive, as it resembles an accusatory or commanding gesture. The polite alternative is to gesture with an open hand or use a subtle nod of the head. This norm is widely observed across all social settings in France.
local_tip: Instead of pointing, gesture with your whole hand, palm up, or use a slight chin lift to indicate a person or object.

also_check.note: Pointing with the index finger is very rude; use an open hand or a gentle wave instead.
Pointing is acceptable in casual contexts but can be seen as confrontational in formal settings.
Pointing with the index finger is offensive; use the thumb or an open hand to indicate direction.
